title: Sadar Bazaar Delhi: Timings, What to Buy and Wholesale Shopping Guide
summary: Complete guide to Sadar Bazaar Delhi. Timings 10 AM to 7 PM, Sunday closed, what each section sells, Diwali decorations, toys, Dhanteras utensils and wholesale pricing.
body_markdown:
Sadar Bazaar is not a single market. It is a wholesale district made up of several interconnected markets, each specialising in a different product category.


- **Swadeshi Market** handles toys, artificial jewellery, gift items and Diwali decorations.
- **Narain Market** handles crockery, kitchenware, steel utensils and Dhanteras items.
- **Pratap Market** handles cosmetics and beauty products.
- **Teliwara** handles timber and construction hardware.


The lanes between them carry everything from stationery to festive decorations to household plastics. Most retail shops across Delhi and neighbouring states source their stock from this market.


## **Quick Reference**


**Detail** **Information**


**Timings** 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday to Saturday


**Weekly off** Sunday


**Nearest metro** Pulbangash (Red Line), about 10 minutes on foot


**Parking** Extremely limited; metro or auto-rickshaw recommended


**Bargaining** Expected, particularly for non-branded and bulk items


**Payment** Cash preferred at most shops; UPI at larger establishments


## **How Sadar Bazaar Pricing Works**


This is a wholesale market first and a retail destination second. Every shop is set up to sell in bulk, and the per-unit pricing reflects that structure.


A simple example: a box of 50 earthen diyas at sadar bazaar delhi costs less than a packet of 10 diyas at a neighbourhood retail store. That gap is what brings small shopkeepers, event planners, school supply buyers, housing society committees and festival decorators here from across Delhi NCR and neighbouring states.


Retail buyers are welcome at almost every shop. You can buy a single item, but the price per piece drops with quantity. The wholesale discount typically starts at:


- 10+ units for small items (diyas, candles, toys)
- 50+ units for bulk decoration items
- 100+ units for stationery and packaging


## **Swadeshi Market: Toys, Gifts and Artificial Jewellery**


Swadeshi Market is the section inside Sadar Bazaar that most retail visitors gravitate towards. It carries the widest variety of consumer products in the complex.


### **Toys**


The toy section runs across several lanes and carries everything from imported action figures to traditional Indian board games, educational toys, soft toys and novelty items. During Diwali and Christmas, the toy inventory expands significantly.


Delhi’s[Toy and Baby Products Association](https://www.toyfair.in/) lists Sadar Bazaar as one of the primary wholesale toy hubs in North India. For school fairs, birthday party return gifts and festive season stocking, this is where the supply chain starts.


### **Gift Items and Festival Stock**


During the Diwali season (roughly October through November), the gift item section of Swadeshi Market expands to include:


- Decorative candle sets and designer diya plates
- Photo frames and wall hangings
- Corporate gift packaging and hamper boxes
- Gift wrapping material, ribbons and bags
- Festive return gift sets for Diwali parties


### **Artificial Jewellery**


The artificial jewellery shops along the Swadeshi lanes stock oxidised sets, Kundan imitations, fashion jewellery and matching accessory sets at wholesale rates. During Navratri and wedding season, these shops carry complete sets including earrings, necklaces, bangles and hair accessories.


## **Narain Market: Crockery, Kitchenware and Dhanteras Shopping**


Narain Market is the crockery and kitchenware section of Sadar Bazaar. It carries branded and unbranded items side by side.


### **What Narain Market Stocks**


- Steel utensils (plates, glasses, bowls, serving sets)
- Pressure cookers and non-stick cookware
- Ceramic dinner sets and tea sets
- Kitchen tools and gadgets
- Brass items and copper vessels


Prices on branded items here are typically 15 to 25 percent below MRP because the market operates at wholesale volumes.


### **Dhanteras at Narain Market**


Dhanteras ([November 6 in 2026](https://www.drikpanchang.com/) ) is the single busiest day of the year at Narain Market. Buying metal utensils on Dhanteras is considered auspicious across North India, and the demand peaks sharply on this one day.


If you plan to shop at Narain Market on Dhanteras, arrive before 11 AM. By afternoon, the lanes are congested, queues extend into the connecting alleys, and the browsing experience becomes difficult.


## **Diwali Decorations**


This is the category that makes Sadar Bazaar the default Diwali shopping destination for a large part of Delhi. The decoration stock appears roughly two to three weeks before the festival and runs until the stock is cleared.


### **What Is Available**


- **Earthen diyas:** From Rs 1 per piece in bulk. The cheapest source in Delhi.
- **Decorative painted diyas:** Rs 5 to Rs 20 each. Hand-painted and designer varieties.
- **LED string lights and rice lights:** Available at wholesale pricing, though Bhagirath Palace nearby is the dedicated lighting market.
- **Torans and bandhanwar:** Decorative door hangings from Rs 50 onwards.
- **Artificial marigold garlands:** Plastic and cloth garlands for home and office decoration.
- **Rangoli stencils and powder colours:** The most comprehensive rangoli supply stock in Delhi.
- **Paper lanterns and kandil:** Multiple sizes and designs.
- **Lakshmi Ganesh idol sets:** Clay (from Rs 20), brass (from Rs 500), silver-plated (from Rs 1,000).


### **When to Shop for Diwali Items**


The widest selection is available 10 to 14 days before Diwali. By the final three days, popular items at the busiest stalls sell out, and the remaining stock carries firmer pricing. The best time to visit is a weekday morning between 10 AM and 12 PM.


## **Stationery and Office Supplies**


The stationery section carries notebooks, registers, pens, files, art supplies and office materials at wholesale rates. Schools, offices and coaching centres across Delhi NCR source annual supplies from this section.


This zone is less relevant for Diwali shopping but adds to the market’s year-round utility.


## **What Sadar Bazaar Does Not Sell**


Understanding the boundaries saves wasted time:


- **Branded electronics, clothing or footwear:** Go to Karol Bagh, Chandni Chowk or Lajpat Nagar.
- **Festive ethnic wear:** Chandni Chowk for traditional, Lajpat Nagar for mid-range, Sarojini for budget.
- **Sweets and dry fruit gift boxes:** Chandni Chowk halwai lane or Chawri Bazaar.
- **LED lighting and electrical decorations at scale:** Bhagirath Palace (adjacent, often combined in one trip).


## **Practical Tips for Visiting**


Sadar Bazaar is not an air-conditioned shopping experience. The lanes are narrow, crowded and hot during warmer months. Porter carts move through the same lanes as shoppers.


- Carry your own bags rather than expecting packaging at every shop.
- Wear comfortable shoes. The lanes are uneven.
- Avoid Saturday afternoons, which are the busiest period of the week.
- During festival weeks, some shops open on Sundays (their regular off day), but this is not guaranteed.
- Metro to Pulbangash station is the practical approach. Street parking is extremely difficult.


## **How to Combine With Bhagirath Palace**


Bhagirath Palace, the wholesale electrical market, sits adjacent to the Sadar Bazaar area in the Chandni Chowk zone. A combined morning visit covering Sadar Bazaar for decorations and puja items, then Bhagirath Palace for LED lighting, covers the two largest Diwali shopping categories in a single 3 to 4 hour trip.


Check the[Jaipur bus booking page](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/jaipur-bus-booking-online) for current schedules if you are visiting Delhi from Rajasthan for wholesale or festival shopping.


***Note:*** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is sadar bazaar delhi famous for?**


Sadar Bazaar is Delhi’s largest wholesale market, known for toys, household items, stationery, cosmetics, festive decorations and gift items at wholesale pricing.


### **What are the timings of Sadar Bazaar?**


10:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday through Saturday. The market is closed on Sundays.


### **Is Sadar Bazaar open on Sunday?**


Sadar Bazaar is closed on Sundays. During Diwali week, some shops may open on Sunday but this is not guaranteed.


### **Which metro station is nearest to Sadar Bazaar?**


Pulbangash metro station on the Red Line, approximately 10 minutes on foot from the main market entrance.


### **Is Sadar Bazaar good for Diwali shopping?**


Sadar Bazaar is Delhi’s primary wholesale source for Diwali decorations, offering diyas, torans, rangoli materials and decoration items at the lowest prices in the city.


### **Can I buy single items or is it bulk-only?**


Most shops sell single items to retail buyers. Pricing is structured for wholesale, but even single-piece purchases are cheaper than retail shops.


### **What is the difference between Sadar Bazaar and Chandni Chowk?**


Sadar Bazaar specialises in wholesale household goods, toys and decorations. Chandni Chowk covers textiles, jewellery, wedding trims and food.


### **When is the best time to visit for Diwali items?**


Visit 10 to 14 days before Diwali for the widest selection. The final 3 days see sellouts and firmer pricing. Weekday mornings are least crowded.


### **Is Bhagirath Palace near Sadar Bazaar?**


Bhagirath Palace is adjacent in the Chandni Chowk area. A combined visit covers decorations at Sadar Bazaar and lighting at Bhagirath Palace in one trip.


### **What should I carry when visiting Sadar Bazaar?**


Carry cash, wear comfortable shoes, bring your own bags, and arrive on a weekday morning for the least crowded and most productive shopping experience.
